title: Stance Adverbs: Commenting on Facts About a Writer

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know stance adverbs such as *afortunadamente*, *lamentablemente*, *en realidad* and *en rigor* from B2 Unit 1. They step outside the sentence and show how the speaker sees a fact, and a comma marks each edge. A text about a writer's life is a good place for them: they correct what readers expect (*en realidad*), give the exact truth (*en rigor*) or show a feeling about a fact (*afortunadamente*).

sections.title: Four stance adverbs
rows: En realidad, empezó su carrera como periodista.
*en realidad*: in fact, correcting what people expect
En rigor, Macondo no es Aracataca.
Afortunadamente, sus textos periodísticos se han reunido en libros.
Lamentablemente, no todos sus textos se conservan.

items.spanish: En realidad, García Márquez empezó su carrera como periodista.
items.english: In fact, García Márquez began his career as a journalist.

items.spanish: En rigor, Macondo no es un pueblo real, sino un lugar de ficción.
items.english: Strictly speaking, Macondo is not a real town but a place in fiction.

items.spanish: Afortunadamente, el periódico conserva los textos que se publicaron en 1955.
items.english: Fortunately, the newspaper keeps the texts that were published in 1955.

items.spanish: El autor, en realidad, nació en un pueblo pequeño de la costa caribe.
items.english: The author, in fact, was born in a small town on the Caribbean coast.

sections.content: Try the comma test: if you can pause and put commas round the adverb, it is commenting on the whole sentence. Use one stance adverb per sentence; two in a row sound heavy. This text is about the writer and his work: it states facts and attributes judgements.
